reissued: Second form, written on lane/d-book-integrate after the game designer decided every call and an adversarial check corrected the decisions. The first form asked Tyler 135 questions. This form asks him for five short lists.
source: docs/design/overhaul/decisions/all.json (one row a call), docs/design/overhaul/decisions/review.md (the adversarial check) and docs/design/overhaul/00-the-game.md (the front of the book)
vision: You run four heroes from your first day. They hunt while you are away, and you win by preparing them: who stands where, what they wear, what their bars do and where you send them. Every choice is made once and remembered. Harder tiers ask for a real party with a tank and a healer. Gear is a chase with rare finds worth keeping. Levels never end, and gear, sinks and old grounds keep pace by formula. Around the hunt stands a shared world that works while everyone sleeps: clans, world bosses, events and two arenas, paying buffs and gear. Crowns buy Premium, looks and comfort, and trade to other players for gold. That gold is the edge, under one ceiling written in numbers that a player who never pays can also reach. Every number comes from formulas you can read.

ruled.what: All four heroes from the start. No slot prices. (GR-2)
One Premium for each account.
No solo or group balance targets. Party buffs make hunting together the obvious choice. (GR-67)
The four together, on the tier they can hold, earn more for each hero than the same four split up. A lone hero is a slower choice, never a trap.
The MMO layer is clans, world bosses, events and PvP arenas, and it is heavy work going forward.
Decisions first. No build lanes until every decision is made and a build plan exists.
Buying Crowns and selling them for gold gives real advantages, just not broken ones.
The MMO layer rewards buffs and gear, because that is what drives players to buy Crowns and sell them for gold.
Two PvP arenas: one with normalized stats and one that uses your gear.
The current game is irrelevant. Nothing is compared with it. Its data is evidence only.
Balance is fixed at the formula layer. No ground, weapon or monster gets its own patch or its own math.
Nothing planned for later is cut. It is built later and stays hidden until it works.
The itemization plan is a source of record.
Every time number assumes a player hunts 12 hours a day, measured in low, mid and best gear, to Level 400.
The Level table is the clock of a mid-geared four on the hardest tier it holds.
Level 400 takes 4,580 hunted hours, which is day 382.
Best gear is about 15% faster and takes about 15% less damage than mid gear.
A death costs 6% of all Level XP, flat, with no cap.
The harder tiers kill at a flat count at every Level. A mid-geared party on Deadly dies 50 to 100 times in 1,000 hours.
The weekly limits on chest opens stay.
120 days of grounds at Early Access, and each region opens 30 days before the first fours arrive.
The Luck bar keeps its hours: +16% at 500 hours, +39% at 5,000.
A player may cost at most $0.15 an account a month at 1,000 accounts, and no more at 10,000.
Bought gold has no limit on how much sooner. The limit is on what can be bought.
Two visits a day is the free game.
Heroes work in town for all 12 rested hours.
A full set of the best gear takes about one band to Krell, then one to two regions.
Crafting is a quarter to a half of the step from mid gear to best gear, and a player who never crafts can buy it.
The too strong and too weak thresholds stand, and any cut goes to you on one list first.
One Global chat, with lines sent in small batches and a slow mode when crowded.
Clan castle goods keep their prices. Only the two goods that cannot be made are fixed.
A unique can be reforged up a band and keeps its property. Each new band also gets uniques of its own.
The every-idle-hour training reading is a number we watch, never a gate.
Faction skills are sized to matter.
Spells are sized first, then Deadly.
Storm and Bone runes unlock at Runecrafting 25 and 40.
Cleave merges into Turning Cut.
Rend stays at 6 seconds and the axes do not hold Power Strike.
Mend heals about 11% of max health.
The hammer has its own strike that spends an Earth rune.
The crossbow has its own spell list. Sixteen Necrotic and Storm spells in all.
Only people are weak to Necrotic.
Every spell is sized at Level 10 and at Level 60, so heals and first strikes land whole in the first hours.
Krell is weeks away, not months: day 18 for a four.
The recommended option of every call in the four dives of 11-20 is approved.
Tempering carries up a tier and costs only the difference.
Generous drops through Krell, really rare and strong after.
Luck has two feeds and no more: rivets used and Bestiary stages.
The harder tiers hit harder, sized on a party with a healer and monsters that shoot the back row.

tyler.note: The only things that need Tyler. Everything else is decided.

money.recommendation: Yes. Paying gives a real edge under one ceiling written in numbers. A player who does not pay reaches the same ceiling with gold.

Crowns buy Premium, looks and comfort. Two timed boosts, damage +6% and protection of about 3%, are sold for gold in 1 day and 7 day sizes, priced on the wage curve and burned. If you want stronger Crown demand, the same two are sold for Crowns and that becomes reversal 24.
No. No Level XP boost is sold, for Crowns or for gold.
Yes. The same rows and the same caps. One bought boost on a knob at a time.
Keep ruling 50-11. Record one reading held by a test: 1.65 with every cap full, about 1.22 from paying alone.
Yes. Paying puts a hero 0 bands ahead, and inside a band at most best gear over mid gear.
Yes. The weekly cap on Crowns an account sells is worth about one account-week of hunting gold, re-derived each week from the 7 day median price.

money.call: The path for players who do not pay
money.recommendation: Yes. Everything sold for Crowns can be had with gold through the book. Premium for a month targets about 3 account-days of gold.
Yes. A number on the account, one server-owned book, fixed lots, one trade then bound, 1% to list and 4% of the gold, both burned. Named "Crown Exchange".
Yes. The eight clamps, with gold paid for Crowns counted against the market's daily spend cap, all inside the one Security review before Early Access.
Yes. The Even Arena, events, and access to any Level, ground, drop or tier. The Open Arena reads bought boosts on purpose.
Everything in the layer is open to every account. Premium banks arena tickets to 30. Premium does not make buffs last longer.

money.call: What one Premium gives four heroes
money.recommendation: The ruled list (12 hour bar on every hero, the full analyzer, looks and a free color change a day, 100 listings for 14 days), the daily claim with no press, one daily 1 hour training item for each hero, tickets to 30.

money.call: The price of Premium and a Crown
money.recommendation: 30 days, priced in Crowns, at 8 to 10 dollars a month as a number to react to. Lot sizes are set so MM-34 holds at the opening price.
Free for everyone: how close a hunt came to a death and deaths per 100 hours for the ground and tier. Premium keeps the full analyzer, as ruled in 24-4.

grant.call: Test Crowns in the playtest. THIS IS A GRANT
grant.recommendation: Yes, for the wiped Discord playtest only. The same amount for every account, one server switch that is off by default and removed before Early Access, every grant journalled. It needs your explicit yes.

moneyLater.call: An always-on engine server, before 10,000 accounts. LATER. A spend, not decided
moneyLater.recommendation: Nothing to buy now. The edge fits the beta and 1,000 accounts. Decide it before 10,000 accounts. ESTIMATED by study 48: at 10,000 accounts an account with a tab open 3.5 hours costs 30.3 database-seconds a day on the edge against a budget of 24, and 9.1 on an engine server. With the browser closed it is 10.0 against 3.5. It is the only way an account that watches fits 24, and it makes a shared fight cheap. Its cost in money is not in the study.

reversals.change: Past the third Blessing a new one opens whenever a fully blessed death would cost over five hunted hours. An unblessed death is untouched.
reversals.ruling: 50-4 of 2026-11-21 (6% flat, no cap, and the 12 hour blessed cap turned down), and the three Blessings of 2026-11-10
reversals.reason: Without it a death past about Level 100 costs so many hours that nobody would press Deadly.

reversals.change: Krell's Hold is day 31 for the plain mid-geared four.
reversals.reason: The Level table ruled the same day puts Level 85 on day 31, and both cannot be exact.

reversals.change: The four runs 106 hours ahead of the table. Level 100 at 494 hours, Level 400 on day 373.
reversals.ruling: The table of 2026-10-25, and "Level 400 is day 382" of 2026-11-21
reversals.reason: Levels 1 to 50 stay timed on a lone new hero, so a four gains 106 hours there and keeps them.

reversals.change: Staged content ends on day 116.
reversals.ruling: "120 days of grounds at Early Access" of 2026-11-21
reversals.reason: It follows from the row above. It is not a reversal if the top staged band runs to Level 189, which is the plan.

reversals.change: A gear band is a fixed step of the curve, opening at about +17%. Luck's two numbers are keyed by Level.
reversals.ruling: The item plan section 2 (two bands a region, 2026-11-18), a major upgrade every 15 to 25 Levels (2026-10-25), the Luck step of 2026-11-20
reversals.reason: A fixed step lets gear keep pace with Levels that never end, with no table typed by hand.

reversals.change: Tempering, Hallmark and lining prices are a share of a band's gold.
reversals.reason: A share holds the size asked for that day at every Level, where a typed price goes stale.

reversals.change: The hammer's Earth rune strike breaks a monster's spell windup.
reversals.reason: It gives the hammer a job in a party, and it touches windups only.

reversals.change: A written spec and five sample Kindling rungs. Nothing is built.
reversals.reason: Two tanks need a way to differ past the last rune tier, and paper costs nothing.

reversals.change: The boss call and the daily roll fold into keyed halls.
reversals.reason: Two doors to one boss is one decision asked twice.

reversals.change: The 4% is the total of always-on perks. A matched hero gains at most 8%.
reversals.reason: A perk that only works in one case has to be bigger than 4% to be worth a slot.

reversals.change: The yard's rate follows the skill curve, capped at half of hunting.
reversals.reason: A flat rate is too strong early and worthless late. This is close to the alternative Tyler passed over.

reversals.change: The market is open on day one.
reversals.reason: Four heroes and Crowns for gold both need a market from the first day.

reversals.change: Setup slots are free.
reversals.reason: A saved setup is a remembered decision, and charging for it sells the first principle.

reversals.change: Three home looks, and visiting opens from the Homestead.
reversals.reason: Three looks can be drawn well, and visiting is worth more the earlier it opens.

reversals.change: Deeds, room rungs and chests are re-priced for an account of four.
reversals.ruling: The gold numbers of 26-3 and 26-1 of 2026-11-20
reversals.reason: The numbers were typed for one hero's income, and an account now has four.

reversals.change: Town work moves on screen in real time and the server writes at the start, at each paid hour and at a stop.
reversals.reason: It looks the same to the player, and study 48 shows no design meets the server budget without it (worth 109 database-seconds an account-day, ESTIMATED).

reversals.change: The Hearthrise lights on the calendar's weekend, sized by the fire. (One row with GR-82.)
reversals.reason: A known weekend can be planned around, and the fire still decides how big it is.

reversals.change: No hired, lent or on-call heroes.
reversals.reason: Every account has four heroes of its own, so a hired seat has no job.

reversals.change: The castle is priced for each member with a floor of five, one project at a time, open at any size.
reversals.reason: Clans now pay buffs, so a fixed price would lock a small clan out of hero power. Tyler declined this option once.

reversals.change: The in-between ground weekend features named pieces in place of XP.
reversals.reason: It keeps Level XP events rare and gives gear a weekend.

reversals.change: No Local chat tab and no live party finder.
reversals.reason: Both need two players at the screen in the same minute, which an idle game rarely has.

reversals.change: One visible two thirds line for mixed Levels.
reversals.reason: A rule the player can read replaces a hidden cut. The ruled parts are untouched.

reversals.change: A clan hunt is two rooms on one pool.
reversals.reason: It keeps every fight a party of four, which is what the engine and the formulas are built on.

serverCost.answer: The target game fits $0.15 an account a month at 1,000 accounts. At 10,000 accounts it fits for an account that does not watch a hunt, and misses by about a third for one that does unless the engine runs on an always-on server.

serverCost.decided: GR-1: town work paid in closed form (worth 109 database-seconds a day, ESTIMATED), and a closed hunt saved every 10 minutes or at 1.2 seconds of engine time (the result is MEASURED identical at every cadence).

then: The build plan: one plan orders the work so each formula lands before the systems that read it.
The build: lanes follow that plan, each change proven on the balance matrix before the next one leans on it.
The release: one big release for the beta, then the wipe and Early Access after the full Security review.
